title: TS-45 Host re-gates run_terminal (security gap)
description:
Source: the fresh re-audit report at /tmp/ts/reaudit.md (read the per-feature blocks for your features). Rules: features stay the spec (Gherkin text of existing scenarios unchanged); cucumber-js steps drive production code; every fixed or new scenario group gets a recorded mutation check (break production, scenario fails, restore); no new Python; push with an explicit refspec (git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>), never plain git push.

The TS regate protocol covers only browse, read and write, so run_terminal is not re-gated at the host: the Python-era scenario 'A tampered continuation job is re-gated before execute' (features/agent_terminal_host_worker.feature, the tampered terminal scenario, currently off the manifest) has no TS equivalent. Add a terminal kind to the host-protocol schemas and the control plane regate (conversation/src/http/host.ts, host-protocol/src/schemas.ts, domain/actions.ts), have the host terminal executor call regate before executing, then port that scenario with a mutation check (skip the terminal regate, the scenario fails) and add it to the manifest. Also verify the TS side re-gates with the SAME grant the turn holds (a command outside the grant is refused at the host).

comments.author: home
comments.text: Merged via PR 443. run_terminal is now re-gated at the host with the turn's grant.

right_now_summary: run_terminal now re-gates at the host using the turn’s grant, and commands outside that grant are refused.
